reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that rapid synthesis can produce well-mixed high-entropy nanoalloys and that slow kinetics cause phase segregation, but it does not provide specific evidence that rapid synthesis induces lattice distortion, that this distortion creates local disorder, or that such disorder retards diffusion and prevents segregation. The key mechanistic premises are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Rapid synthesis creates large lattice distortion in high-entropy nanoalloys
Lattice distortion creates strong local atomic disorder
Local atomic disorder retards atomic diffusion
Retarded diffusion prevents phase segregation at high temperatures
Slow synthesis yields lower lattice distortion and thus less stability
